difficulty_notes: Requires multi-step NPV math and weighing qualitative implementation factors with some exhibit synthesis, but scope is contained and ambiguity lower than Hard anchors.

Short Darden profitability case aimed at beginners (0-10 cases). Math likely limited to simple cost/price break-evens and capacity, with one or two straightforward exhibits. Options (improve, repurpose, divest) add some synthesis but remain well-structured and low-ambiguity, making it easier than the medium anchors like Copier Co.

Requires multi-step 5-year revenue forecast and integration of market, competitive, consumer and sustainability factors, but math is labeled easy and exhibits are limited to ~12 pages, so overall comparable to a solid but not extreme MBB case.
Very qualitative brainstorm-style growth case with minimal data and math; only requires segment comparison and strategic fit discussion, similar to Easy anchors like Zephyr Beverages.

One core compounding math segment plus strategic gap-filling; moderate ambiguity and synthesis similar to other standard PE profitability cases, lighter than Hard anchors but more involved than Easy ones.

Standard Bain R1 market-sizing + breakeven profitability case. Math is light (basic % multiplications, replacement rate) and qualitative considerations are typical industry/fit/risk points; some ambiguity with the two-part stem but overall comparable to medium anchors like Copier Co.

Requires a full before-vs-after financial comparison with a market-sizing, revenue impact, multiple cost buckets, and working-capital cash-flow element, but exhibits keep data light and structure is hinted by the prompt. Similar complexity to standard Kellogg/Darden medium cases, short of the data density and ambiguity seen in hard MBB finals.
